head: claude/mi92-claudebot-command-menu
title: MI-92 follow-up: make the ClaudeBot command MENU populate, and make the outcome readable
body:
## Summary

`/status` and `/decisions` **answer** on ClaudeBot (the operator ran `/status` at 08:23:05Z and got the full manager status) but the composer's **Menu button does not offer them**. Operator: *"I want the menu to open up on the menu button in the chat, not just by typing. I should be able to click to open the menu and then choose the command I want."*

The handlers are fine. The **discoverable surface** was not.

## One cause is ELIMINATED by evidence, not by theory

The manager flagged that `_post_init` logged nothing on success, so the journal could not distinguish *set them* / *never ran* / *failed*. That ambiguity is real and is fixed here — but the **never-ran** branch closes without the token:

- `telegram.ext.Application.post_init` is a plain **slot attribute**, not a property (checked against the installed **PTB 22.8**), so `app.post_init = _post_init` after `.build()` **is** honoured.
- `run_polling` executes it: `if self.post_init: loop.run_until_complete(self.post_init(self))`.
- The 08:00:46Z restart reached `Application started` with **zero** Traceback/Exception/ERROR lines, and a raising `post_init` would propagate out of `run_polling` and crash-loop under `Restart=always`.

**So the call RAN and returned without error.** Not never-ran, not failed.

## What that leaves — and this does not guess between them

Three candidates remain: command **SCOPE**, the chat **MENU BUTTON** type, and **client-side caching** of a list first published only that morning (which no code can fix).

**1. The menu button — the best-supported candidate.** Nothing in this repo had **ever** called `setChatMenuButton` (grepped: zero hits), so this bot's button was whatever BotFather left it as. `default` behaves as `commands`, but a `web_app` button does **not** list commands however correctly they are published. The trader bot runs the *same* `set_my_commands` code path and its menu works — so the difference between the two bots is per-bot config, not code. Now set explicitly, with `chat_id` omitted so it sets the **default** button for every private chat rather than patching one chat.

**2. The outcome is now READ BACK from Telegram, not asserted.** The startup reads **before** and **after** — both scopes in the private-chat resolution chain plus the menu button type — and logs what came back. The `before` read is what **names the cause** on the next restart. This is the same class MI-83 fixed for merge-pings: the branch nobody logs is the branch nobody can verify.

## ⚠️ A correction I made to my own change, in place

The first draft justified the `all_private_chats` write with this comment:

> *"an empty specific scope does not fall back — it wins"*

**That is false.** Per the Bot API's documented resolution, `chat → all_private_chats → default` takes the first **non-empty** list, so an empty specific scope **does** fall back. I nearly shipped a fabricated cause as the justification for a write.

The write is **kept**, for a different and true reason: we cannot see from here whether that scope is empty, and a **non-empty** `all_private_chats` would **shadow** the default-only write this bot has always done. It is **defensive, not a diagnosis** — and the before-read is what will actually settle it. The comment now says exactly that, including what it used to say and why that was wrong.

## Safety

Failures are logged at **ERROR** and **never raised**, in **two independent `try` blocks**. `post_init` runs inside `run_polling`, so raising would abort startup — and under `Restart=always` that turns a **cosmetic menu problem into a crash-loop on the channel carrying the operator's decisions**. Answering `/status` matters more than showing it in a menu. Independent wrapping means one call's failure cannot suppress the other.

The body was extracted from a closure in `main()` into a module-level `publish_command_surface(bot)` returning a diagnostic dict, so the failure paths are testable rather than reachable only by starting polling.

## Constraints held

- `HANDLED_PREFIXES` stays `(CB_PREFIX,)` — commands are `CommandHandler`s, not `callback_query` traffic.
- **The trader bot is untouched.** MI-92's constraint stands and is verified honoured on the fleet (trader restarted 08:01:16Z, zero `operator_commands` lines).

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — two Bot-API calls at startup on one bot; no schema, pipeline stage, public API, or inter-process contract changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_operator_commands.py` — **27 passed** (was 20). Seven new, against a hand-written fake rather than a `MagicMock` (an auto-speccing mock answers every attribute, so a typo'd method name would pass silently):
  - the menu button is set to `commands`, with `chat_id` **omitted** so it is the default for all private chats;
  - commands go to **both** `all_private_chats` and the default scope;
  - `commands_live` / `menu_before` / `menu_after` come from **read-backs**, not from what was sent — asserted with a `web_app` button so the cause-naming path is exercised;
  - **both scopes are read BEFORE writing**, so a shadowing list is visible;
  - **parametrized both ways:** either call failing leaves the other intact, does not raise, and still logs loudly;
  - `post_init` is reachable — `Application.post_init` is not a read-only property, and `main()` delegates to the tested function rather than inlining a second copy.
- [x] `test_telegram_query_bot.py`, `test_menu.py`, `test_telegram_decisions.py`, `test_manager_status.py`, `test_operator_commands.py` — **209 passed, 4 skipped**.
- [x] `pr-landing-guard` — `OK — state=declared_needs_approval`.
- [ ] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` — full run in progress at time of writing; CI's `guards` job is the authoritative verdict.
- [ ] **CI green** — pending.
- [ ] ⚠️ **THE DONE-CONDITION IS THE OPERATOR SEEING THE MENU.** No harness can reach it, and neither can a journal line: a log saying the button was set is not the button rendering in a Telegram client. **Only the operator can confirm this one.**

## ⛔ What needs the operator's OK

**Tier-2** (`src/bot/`, needs an `ict-claude-decision-bot.service` restart). Landing declared `hold` / `tier_2_3_needs_approval`. **This session merges nothing.**

1. One operator OK to merge.
2. Restart `ict-claude-decision-bot.service` (the trader bot is **not** involved this time — no both-bots window).
3. **Read the journal, which now answers the question:** `/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-decision-bot.service` will carry `menu button was <X>, now 'commands'`. If `<X>` is `web_app`, that **was** the cause and the line says so explicitly. It also prints the two scopes as they were before the write.
4. Then open the ClaudeBot chat and tap the Menu button.

⚠️ **If the menu is still empty after that**, the remaining candidate is client-side caching, which no code change can fix — the log will have ruled the other two out by then, which is the point of the read-back.
